qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Proposals (RFP) issued by AmeriCorps NCCC for organizations to apply for teams to perform community service projects. It includes application instructions, project focus areas, and partner responsibilities, indicating a procurement opportunity.

quotes.quote: How Do You Apply for a Team?

findings.title: Eligible Applicant Organizations
findings.fact: Qualifying organizations include nonprofit and faith-based organizations, government entities, public schools and universities, and Native American tribal councils.
findings.business_implication: Only these types of organizations are eligible to apply for an AmeriCorps NCCC team.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that your organization falls into one of these categories before applying.

quotes.quote: Qualifying organizations include: • Nonprofit and faith-based organizations • Government entities (federal, state, and local) • Public schools and universities • Native American tribal councils

findings.title: Application Process
findings.fact: Applications are handled by Assistant Program Directors (APDs). To apply, determine project dates, contact NCCCProjectApplications@AmeriCorps.gov, follow instructions to submit a complete application by the due date, and make the application stand out.
findings.business_implication: The application process is initiated via email and requires a complete submission by the due date.
findings.action_recommendation: Contact the provided email to obtain application instructions and ensure all required elements are included.

quotes.quote: Applications are handled by Assistant Program Directors (APDs). To apply: • Determine the project dates when you’d like to receive a team. • Contact us by emailing NCCCProjectApplications@AmeriCorps.gov. • Follow the instructions to submit a complete application by the due date. • Make your application stand out! (See page 2.)

findings.title: Award Notification Timeline
findings.fact: Applicants will be notified of award approximately six weeks prior to the project start date.
findings.business_implication: The award notification timeline is relative to the project start date, not a fixed date.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan project start dates with the six-week notification period in mind.

quotes.quote: We will notify applicants of award approximately six weeks prior to the project start date.

findings.title: Partner Organization Responsibilities
findings.fact: Partner organizations must provide at least 40 hours per week of enriching service, daily technical supervision, all project materials, tools, protective gear, work permits, housing with full kitchen and bathroom, and other specified items.
findings.business_implication: The partner organization must have the capacity to provide these resources and supervision.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess your organization's ability to meet these requirements before applying.

quotes.quote: What Do Partner Organizations Provide? • At least 40 hours per week of enriching service that meets the needs named in your application • A broad range of different types of service experiences for the team • Daily technical supervision for the team, including on-the-job training • Orientation to the organization and community • All project materials, tools, and protective gear • Any work permits required to complete service • Service-learning education on community needs and deeper issues related to the project • Housing for the team, to include a full kitchen, full bathroom with showers, cleaning supplies, and toilet paper for the duration of the project
